title: Tenant saturation patterns and eviction tuning proposal
body:
Context:
We keep seeing recurrent "tenant saturation" episodes on dedicated GPU pools that manifest as: rising tail latency for small inference requests, spiky scheduler backpressure, and sudden eviction cascades that pull critical production jobs off GPU nodes. These are distinct from hardware faults — pattern indicates workload packing + bursty long-seq tenants that cause KV-cache amplification and allocator thrash.

Purpose of this doc:
- Capture observed saturation patterns from Nov–Dec 2024 incidents (summary below).
- Propose an eviction scoring tweak and autoscaler config changes to reduce cascading evictions.
- Draft an on-call playbook for isolating noisy tenants quickly and safely.
- Define an experiment and rollback plan to validate changes on a single pool before wider rollout.

High-level hypothesis (short):
- Root cause: a small number of tenants run sporadic long-context prompts that cause memory/kv cache pressure + prolonged GPU kernels, increasing per-node scheduling delay. Current eviction thresholds are tuned to CPU-based containers, not persistent attention-state workloads, so the allocator misclassifies pressure and evicts stable low-throughput tenants, causing throughput oscillation.

Incident summary (most recent SRE-8421):
- 2024-11-12 02:14 UTC: first alert — pool "dedicated-west-3a-14" tail_p95 latency spike > 2.4s for 6 minutes.
- 02:18 UTC: autoscale attempted to add nodes; scale up throttled due to quota in region.
- 02:20 UTC: allocator reported sustained backpressure events (event type: SCHED_BACKPRESSURE) and started eviction cycle at 02:24 UTC.
- 02:24–02:40 UTC: eviction cascade — 7 tenants evicted in <16m, two were internal low-latency routing consumers.
- 02:40 UTC: traffic reroute to fallback model variants; latency recovered, but customer-visible errors occurred for 18 minutes.

Key signals observed (metrics / traces):
- Node GPU util: 65–98% (high variance) with frequent 10–30s stalls.
- GPU memory pressure: >92% during burst windows.
- KV cache miss ratio spike from 2% baseline to 37% for affected model shards.
- Eviction metric: "eviction_score" correlated strongly with per-tenant moving-average of kernel-duration * mem_pressure_factor.
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale requests denied by cloud limits.

Why current eviction policy fails:
- Eviction score uses short window (30s) and is dominated by instantaneous GPU utilization spikes that long-seq tasks trigger; short but heavy tenants get labeled as "noisy" and evicted, while tail-traffic continues to cause pressure afterward.
- No explicit backoff for tenants that were recently evicted -> eviction storms.
- No differentiation between long-kernel single-request tenants vs multi-request high-throughput tenants.

Proposed changes (high-level):
1) Eviction score refactor: add "temporal smoothing" and a long-kernel penalty instead of raw instantaneous util. New score = alpha*smoothed_util + beta*(avg_kernel_duration / kernel_duration_baseline) + gamma*mem_pressure_ratio. Provide default alpha/beta/gamma = 0.5/0.35/0.15 (experiment values).
2) Eviction cooldown: add tenant cooldown window (5m) after an eviction decision to prevent immediate re-eviction and cascade.
3) Priority classes: mark internal routing consumers as high-stability tenants (protected tag) so allocator deprioritizes them for eviction unless node becomes critically overloaded (>98% mem + sustained >5m).
4) Autoscaler soft-limits: when cloud quotas block scale-up, raise an emergency routing policy that proactively shifts low-criticality requests to cheaper model variants to reduce mem pressure.
5) Observability additions: new metrics (per-tenant avg_kernel_duration, per-tenant kv_cache_amplification, eviction_cooldown_active) and an alert when eviction rate > X/min and median kernel duration > Y ms.

Draft runbook (on-call immediate steps):
- Pager received: tail latency p95 > 2s on dedicated pool.
- Triage: check pool-level dashboards (GPU util distribution, mem_pressure, eviction_rate).
- Quick isolate (if eviction cascade in progress):
  1) Pause non-critical tenants using the routing-control API: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/pause?pool=<pool>&tag=low-criticality (command in ops toolkit).
  2) If pause not available, add a temporary tenant placement policy: set-allocator-policy --pool <pool> --allow-evict-tag "ephemeral" --protect-tag "routing-infra"
  3) Confirm autoscaler requests and cloud quota state: kubectl get hpa/allocator-autoscaler -n redwood-system and cloud-cli describe quotas.
- If quota prevents scale-up and pressure persists:
  - Activate emergency routing to fallback model variant: /ops/route set-fallback --pool <pool> --percent 30 --duration 15m
- Post-incident: capture heap/gpu-proc samples, KV-cache hit traces for top-3 tenants during spike window. Attach to SRE-8421.

Experiment plan (canary):
- Target pool: dedicated-west-3a-14 (low-traffic during UTC afternoons).
- Step 0: Baseline for 7 days with enhanced tracing enabled (collect per-tenant kernel durations).
- Step 1: Deploy eviction score refactor with alpha/beta/gamma as above, cooldown 5m, protected-tag rules. Rollout to pool at 10:00 UTC, 10% traffic shift test for 1 hour.
- Step 2: Monitor for 48h. Success criteria: 
   - Eviction rate reduced by >= 60% during burst windows,
   - Median p95 latency improvement >= 20%,
   - No increase in SLA failures for protected tenants.
- Rollback criteria: any increase in customer-visible errors > 2x baseline or eviction-induced error window > 10m.

Data to collect for validation:
- Per-tenant time-series: kernel_duration_ms, gpu_mem_used_ratio, kv_cache_miss_rate, eviction_score, eviction_cooldown_active.
- Node-level: scheduling_delay_ms histogram, node_requeue_events, gpu_stall_counts.
- Alert correlation: map eviction events to request traces (trace IDs).

Open questions / risks:
- Risk that smoothing hides short but legitimate spikes (fast bursts that would have been reclaimed by autoscale). Mitigation: keep an absolute hard eviction threshold for critical memory exhaustion.
- Risk of protected tags being misapplied by product teams. Mitigation: limit tag grant to SRE + infra-service accounts and audit weekly.
- Concern: autoscaler soft-limits may over-route traffic to lower-quality variants and impact experience. Mitigation: set percent cap and only allow for non-SLA traffic.

Next steps / action items (owners and due dates):
- Implement metric instrumentation for avg_kernel_duration and kv_cache_amplification (Owner: Daniel Kim) — due 2024-11-28.
- Prototype eviction-score change in allocator branch (Owner: Marco Alvarez) — PR by 2024-12-05.
- Prepare canary pool and runbook automation: add one-click emergency pause button to console (Owner: Priya Gupta) — draft by 2024-12-10.
- Schedule dry-run with oncall team to rehearse playbook (Owner: Aisha Patel) — target 2024-12-16.

Notes to self / scribbles (informal):
- We saw similar pattern on 2024-09-09 but at smaller scale — might be seasonal traffic from marketing campaign. Check product release notes for correlated spikes.
- Consider adding tenant-level rate-limiter for very long-seq single requests (e.g., requests with context > 16k tokens): cap concurrency to 1 and prioritize KV cache retention.

Appendix: quick commands and sample queries
- Find top kernel-duration tenants in last 30m:
  kubectl exec -it allocator-xx -n redwood-system -- allocator-cli top-tenants --metric avg_kernel_duration_ms --window 30m --limit 10
- Eviction cooldown toggle (testing):
  PATCH /allocator/api/config {"eviction_cooldown_ms": 300000} (requires infra-admin)
- Detect cascade pattern in logs (example regex):
  grep -E "evicting tenant|eviction_score" /var/log/allocator/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'

If you're reading this and want to push a change: keep the experiment conservative. We want fewer false positives evictions rather than aggressive early eviction. Document any tagging changes in the tenant taxonomy doc and loop in product for protected-tag approvals.

-- Aisha
